title: The Cloud Who Ate Sadness
markdown:
Rafi Sol’s shop, Echoes & Rewinds, usually buzzed with the low hum of memory scrubbers. Today it felt heavy, like a forgotten gym sock. The front window showed the usual neon of the night market, but the letters seemed tired. A kettle clicked and did not pour. On the counter, a pair of chronoscope goggles sat beside a jar of sugar cubes Rafi used for calibration and, occasionally, tea.

Elara arrived with worry lines like a cosmic map. She set a thin envelope on the glass and did not take her hand off it at once.

“Mr. Sol,” she whispered, voice thin. “My husband. The first time he made me laugh. It’s gone.”

Rafi reached for his steampunk colander-like chronoscope and fitted it over one ear, the way a doctor might listen for a heartbeat that had wandered. The shop’s usual catalog of small embarrassments and misplaced birthdays felt suddenly beside the point.

A sad splat echoed. Mneme, his pet cloud, sagged by the ceiling. Her usual playful swirls were gone, replaced by a dull grey. Sorrowful puffs of vapor fogged the air and beaded on the sugar jar.

“Mneme?” Rafi murmured.

He checked her logs. She had been foraging, appetite strong, yet her energy had plummeted. Where had she been? He traced energetic currents, following a scent on the wind that was not weather. The trail led past the night market’s fried-dough stall, past a fountain that played recorded birdsong, to a row of sterile buildings: Eternal Solace Inc. and Grief-as-a-Service, LLC. Places selling packaged sadness. Display windows showed tasteful grey boxes tied with silver ribbon. A slogan promised closure in under an hour.

Mneme had been feasting on manufactured melancholy.

Rafi’s breath hitched. “Bottled sorrow.” Her delicate system, meant for minor embarrassments, was overwhelmed. He could see it now: she had drifted in through a loading vent, curious, and found a banquet.

He grabbed a contraption, an antique humidifier crossed with an atmospheric processor, and wheeled it under her sagging belly.

“Come on, girl,” he soothed.

He flipped a switch. Iridescent mist swirled. The processor whirred, condensing the dark particles into tiny harmless droplets that ran into a tray like ordinary rain. The oppressive weight lifted. Mneme’s opalescent colors returned, a little at a time, like someone remembering a joke. She puffed back, light and playful, and knocked a sugar cube onto the floor as if to prove she was herself.

Elara gasped. “That device?”

Rafi grinned, then thought better of a lecture. “She ate the wrong weather. True memories are messy. That stuff in the boxes is just weight.” He wiped a droplet from the chronoscope. “We process feelings. We don’t rent them.”

He turned the colander toward Elara’s envelope. The first laugh was still there, thin as a hair, stuck under a layer of someone else’s grief. He teased it free the way he would a scratch on a record. Elara’s mouth opened. She did not describe the joke. She only laughed once, startled and real, and Mneme, tasting nothing manufactured in it, did a small delighted loop under the neon and left the sugar where it lay.
characters: Rafi Sol (black-market memory restorer), Mneme (memory-eating pet cloud)
